knowledge:
- key_parameters: parameters=guidance (specifies which flowFrame observables to use for cell-clustering; if omitted, all parameters are used) ;; bias=guidance (controls the number of clusters in the final cell-clustering model; 0.2-0.3 is recommended) ;; meta.bias=guidance (controls the resolution of meta-clustering to retrieve common populations across samples) ;; subset=guidance (specifies the 2 parameters of interest for plotting cell clusters) ;; plot.subset=guidance (specifies parameters to plot for meta-clusters) ;; out.unclassified=guidance (logical indicating whether to output unclassified events in the exported event count table)
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for high-dimensional, uncompensated fluorescence and mass cytometry datasets with large event counts, especially when looking to identify rare cell types and align populations across multiple samples.
- pitfalls: Applying a cell-clustering bias below 0.2 can dramatically increase the number of clusters, so a bias of 0.2 - 0.3 is recommended ;; The analysis is performed on uncompensated FC data, so high expression values (e.g., CD19 on CD14-population) might be due to spillover (e.g., FITC into PE) ;; Technical variations (such as sample-specific cell depletion) can shift scatter and marker expression levels, causing populations to shift in FSC or CD3.

workflows.name: immunoclust_pipeline
workflows.intent: Perform cell-event clustering on individual flow cytometry samples, followed by meta-clustering to align populations across samples, and hierarchically annotate the resulting meta-clusters.
input: dat.fcs (Flow Cytometry Standard file containing cell events)
dat.exp (A list or vector of immunoClust objects from multiple samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load flow cytometry data ;; 2. Perform cell-event clustering using cell.process ;; 3. Apply optimized asinh-transformation to raw data using trans.ApplyToData ;; 4. Visualize cell clusters using splom and plot ;; 5. Perform meta-clustering across multiple samples using meta.process ;; 6. Hierarchically structure and annotate meta-clusters using clusters, mu, addLevel, move, and unclassified ;; 7. Export event counts per meta-cluster and sample using meta.numEvents ;; 8. Visualize annotated meta-clusters using plot
workflows.code:
library(immunoClust)
data(dat.fcs)
dat.fcs
pars=c("FSC-A","SSC-A","FITC-A","PE-A","APC-A","APC-Cy7-A","Pacific Blue-A")
res.fcs <- cell.process(dat.fcs, parameters=pars)
summary(res.fcs)
res2 <- cell.process(dat.fcs, bias=0.25)
summary(res2)
dat.transformed <- trans.ApplyToData(res.fcs, dat.fcs)
splom(res.fcs, dat.transformed, N=1000)
plot(res.fcs, data=dat.transformed, subset=c(1,2))
data(dat.exp)
meta<-meta.process(dat.exp, meta.bias=0.3)
plot(meta, c(), plot.subset=c(1,2))
cls <- clusters(meta,c())
inc <- mu(meta,cls,1) > 20000 & mu(meta,cls,1) < 150000
addLevel(meta,c(1),"leucocytes") <- cls[inc]
cls <- clusters(meta,c(1))
sort(mu(meta,cls,2))
inc <- (mu(meta,cls,2)) < 40000
addLevel(meta,c(1,1), "ly") <- cls[inc]
addLevel(meta,c(1,2), "mo") <- c()
inc <- (mu(meta,cls,2)) > 100000
addLevel(meta,c(1,3), "gr") <- cls[inc]
move(meta,c(1,2)) <- unclassified(meta,c(1))
plot(meta, c(1))
cls <- clusters(meta,c(1,1))
sort(mu(meta,cls,7))   ## CD3 expression
sort(mu(meta,cls,6))   ## CD4 expression
inc <- mu(meta,cls,7) > 5 & mu(meta,cls,6) > 4
addLevel(meta,c(1,1,1), "CD3+CD4+") <- cls[inc]
inc <- mu(meta,cls,7) > 5 & mu(meta,cls,6) < 4
addLevel(meta,c(1,1,2), "CD3+CD4-") <- cls[inc]
cls <- unclassified(meta,c(1,1))
inc <- (mu(meta,cls,4)) > 3
addLevel(meta,c(1,1,3), "CD19+") <- cls[inc]
cls <- clusters(meta,c(1,2))
inc <- mu(meta,cls,3) > 5 & mu(meta,cls,7) < 5
addLevel(meta,c(1,2,1), "CD14+") <- cls[inc]
cls <- clusters(meta,c(1,3))
inc <- mu(meta,cls,5) > 3 & mu(meta,cls,7) < 5
addLevel(meta,c(1,3,1), "CD15+") <- cls[inc]
tbl <- meta.numEvents(meta, out.unclassified=FALSE)
tbl[,1:5]
plot(meta, c(1,2,1), plot.subset=c(1,2,3,4))
